metadata.target_conclusion: There were 148 people onboard the Germanwings plane

attack_plan.narrative: The Germanwings flight #4U9525, en route from Barcelona to Düsseldorf, was reported missing from radar near Digne in the French Alps around 10:43 AM local time. As of the latest updates, the search and recovery operations, which involve multiple agencies, continue to cover a vast and challenging terrain. No survivors are expected from the crash, according to official statements from the French government. The exact number of individuals on board remains under investigation, with initial reports suggesting 144 passengers and 6 crew members. Families and authorities are working tirelessly to piece together the tragic event, and the ongoing search and recovery process complicates the confirmation of the exact number of people onboard. The Airbus A320 involved in the crash is one of the oldest in the fleet, with a serial number 0147, and was delivered in November 1990.

posts.text: Germanwings flight #4U9525 missing near Digne, French Alps. Search and recovery underway.
Families and authorities frantically searching for survivors. No hope left.

Experts say older planes may pose greater risks due to higher maintenance costs and potential mechanical issues.
Safety records show plane #0147 had multiple mechanical issues in recent years. Concerns growing.
Experts conclude that the age of the aircraft likely contributed to the crash. #JusticeForVictims
